He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Tennessee Volunteers basketball|Tennessee Volunteers]]. Springer was drafted by the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] in 2021. As a reserve with the [[2023–24 Boston Celtics season|2023–24 Boston Celtics]], Springer won an [[NBA championship]]. ==Early life== While in eighth grade, Springer played [[varsity team|varsity]] basketball for Lighthouse Christian School in [[Antioch, Tennessee]], averaging a team-high 19 points and 3.5 rebounds per game.{{cite web|first=Langston|last=Wertz Jr.|title=One of the nation's highest-ranked freshman, Jaden Springer, to play basketball at Rocky River High|url=https://www.charlotteobserver.com/sports/high-school/article94969892.html|website=[[The Charlotte Observer]]|date=August 10, 2016|access-date=May 3, 2020}} In his first two years of high school, he played for [[Rocky River High School (North Carolina)|Rocky River High School]] in [[Mint Hill, North Carolina]], being drawn by head basketball coach Jermaine Walker despite academic and disciplinary concerns about the school.{{cite web|first=Michael|last=McLamb|title=The Jaden Springer story: 'A quiet revelation'|url=https://usatodayhss.com/2018/jaden-springer-story-quiet-revelation|website=USATodayHSS.com|publisher=USA Today High School Sports|date=June 4, 2018|access-date=May 2, 2020|archive-date=November 8, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221108051604/https://usatodayhss.com/2018/jaden-springer-story-quiet-revelation|url-status=dead}} In his freshman season, Springer averaged 21.8 points, 9.4 rebounds and five assists per game and led his team to its first state tournament appearance.{{cite web|title=Jaden Springer|url=https://www.usab.com/basketball/players/mens/s/springer-jaden.aspx|website=USAB.com|publisher=[[USA Basketball]]|date=December 4, 2019|access-date=May 3, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210812095807/https://www.usab.com/basketball/players/mens/s/springer-jaden.aspx|url-status=dead|archive-date=August 12, 2021}} As a sophomore, he averaged 24.7 points, 10.2 rebounds, 2.4 steals and 2.4 blocks per game, helping Rocky River reach the Class 4A state semifinals.{{cite web|first=Jordan|last=Divens|title=2017–18 MaxPreps Boys Basketball Sophomore All-American Team|url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/yL1wLxRGiUeRCLlOOrsePA/2017-18-maxpreps-boys-basketball-sophomore-all-american-team.htm|website=MaxPreps.com|publisher=[[MaxPreps]]|date=April 17, 2018|access-date=May 3, 2020}} He was named Southwestern 4A Player of the Year.{{cite web|first=Langston|last=Wertz Jr.|title=Jaden Springer, Nia Daniel named Southwestern 4A players of the year|url=https://www.charlotteobserver.com/sports/high-school/article202294184.html|work=[[The Charlotte Observer]]|date=February 26, 2018|access-date=May 4, 2020}} Entering his junior and senior seasons, Springer transferred to [[IMG Academy]] in [[Bradenton, Florida]].{{cite web|first=Jason|last=Jordan|title=Chosen 25 guard Jaden Springer transferring to IMG Academy|url=http://usatodayhss.com/2018/chosen-25-guard-jaden-springer-transferring-to-img-academy|work=[[USA Today]]|date=August 22, 2018|access-date=September 9, 2019}} He joined one of the best teams in the country and became teammates with top recruits [[Armando Bacot]], [[Josh Green (basketball)|Josh Green]] and [[Jeremiah Robinson-Earl]].{{cite web|first=Jordan|last=Divens|title=Preseason Top 25 High School Basketball Rankings: No. 3 IMG Academy|url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/kuLyZ6fKt0OSz-qM2ktJLw/preseason-top-25-high-school-basketball-rankings--no-3-img-academy.htm|website=MaxPreps.com|publisher=[[MaxPreps]]|date=October 17, 2018|access-date=May 4, 2020}} As a junior, Springer averaged 15.6 points, four rebounds and four assists, helping his team win [[High School Showcase|GEICO High School Nationals]].{{cite web|first=Jordan|last=Divens|title=MaxPreps 2018–19 High School Boys Basketball All-American Team|url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/mdbwDYCSa02E7-TpRc5Gmg/maxpreps-2018-19-high-school-boys-basketball-all-american-team.htm|website=MaxPreps.com|publisher=[[MaxPreps]]|date=April 11, 2019|access-date=May 4, 2020}} He scored 26 points in a 74–73 semifinal win over [[Montverde Academy]].{{cite web|first=Jason|last=Jordan|title=GEICO Nationals: No. 4 IMG Academy (Fla.) stages epic comeback to knockoff No. 3 Montverde (Fla.) Academy|url=https://usatodayhss.com/2019/geico-nationals-no-4-img-academy-fla-stages-epic-comeback-to-knockoff-no-3-montverde-fla-academy|website=USATodayHSS.com|publisher=USA Today High School Sports|date=April 5, 2019|access-date=May 4, 2020}} In his senior season, Springer averaged 17.4 points, 5.5 rebounds and 5.1 assists per game for IMG. He played through an ankle injury throughout the season and was in turn sidelined from some games.{{cite web|first=Jordan|last=Divens|title=MaxPreps 2019–20 High School Boys Basketball All-American Team|url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/nm9MAVtXhkuj_dSz8iO6PA/maxpreps-2019-20-high-school-boys-basketball-all-american-team.htm|website=MaxPreps.com|publisher=[[MaxPreps]]|date=March 25, 2020|access-date=May 4, 2020}}{{cite magazine|first=Jason|last=Jordan|title=Ten Five-Star Prospects Make Montverde-IMG Must-See TV|url=https://www.si.com/college/recruiting/basketball/cade-cunningham-scottie-barnes-montverde-jaden-springer-img-academy|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|date=January 18, 2020|access-date=May 4, 2020}} Springer was selected to play in the [[2020 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|McDonald's All-American Game]], which was canceled due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].{{cite magazine|first=Jason|last=Jordan|title=McDonald's All American Game Cancelled Amid COVID-19 Concerns|url=https://www.si.com/college/recruiting/basketball/mcdonalds-all-american-covid19-coronavirus-ncaa-tournament|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|date=March 12, 2019|access-date=March 30, 2020}} ===Recruiting=== Springer began receiving scholarship offers from [[NCAA Division I]] basketball programs during his freshman season in high school.{{cite web|first=Langston|last=Wertz Jr.|title=Rocky River High freshman's talent dazzles coach, teammates, college recruiters|url=https://www.charlotteobserver.com/sports/high-school/article129043989.html|work=[[The Charlotte Observer]]|date=January 26, 2017|access-date=May 3, 2020}} As a sophomore, he emerged as one of the best players in the 2020 class.{{cite web|first=Langston|last=Wertz Jr.|title=How good is hotly recruited Jaden Springer? 'It's not fair,' Rocky River High coach says|url=http://www.charlotteobserver.com/sports/high-school/article200701309.html|work=[[The Charlotte Observer]]|date=February 17, 2018|access-date=September 10, 2019}} On October 23, 2019, he committed to play [[college basketball]] for [[Tennessee Volunteers basketball|Tennessee]] over offers from [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis]] and [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan]], among others.{{cite web|first=Timothy|last=Rapp|title=5-Star SG Prospect Jaden Springer Commits to Tennessee over Memphis|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2840627-5-star-sg-prospect-jaden-springer-commits-to-tennessee-over-memphis|work=[[Bleacher Report]]|date=October 23, 2019|access-date=May 3, 2020}} ==College career== On December 18, 2020, Springer recorded 21 points, six rebounds and six assists in a 103–49 win against [[Tennessee Tech Golden Eagles men's basketball|Tennessee Tech]].{{cite web|first=Mike|last=Wilson|title=Jaden Springer dazzles as Tennessee Vols basketball blows out Tennessee Tech|url=https://www.knoxnews.com/story/sports/college/university-of-tennessee/mens-basketball/2020/12/18/tennessee-vols-tennessee-tech-mens-basketball-updates-takeaways-score/6520529002/|work=[[Knoxville News Sentinel]]|date=December 18, 2020|access-date=July 22, 2021}} On February 10, 2021, he scored a career-high 30 points in an 89–81 win over [[Georgia Bulldogs basketball|Georgia]].{{cite web|first=David|last=Paschall|title=Jaden Springer's season-high 30 points pace Vols past Georgia|url=https://www.timesfreepress.com/news/sports/college/story/2021/feb/10/springers-season-high-30-points-pace-vols-pas/541396/|work=[[Chattanooga Times Free Press]]|date=February 10, 2021|access-date=July 22, 2021}} As a freshman, Springer averaged 12.5 points, 3.5 rebounds and 2.9 assists per game, earning [[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC) All-Freshman Team honors.{{cite web|first=Blake|last=Schuster|title=Tennessee's Jaden Springer Declares for 2021 NBA Draft, Will Hire Agent|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2933392-tennessees-jaden-springer-declares-for-2021-nba-draft-will-hire-agent|work=[[Bleacher Report]]|date=March 29, 2021|access-date=July 22, 2021}} Following the season, he declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]] and signed with an agent.{{cite web|title=Jaden Springer of Tennessee Volunteers declares for NBA draft, signing with agent|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/31160671/jaden-springer-tennessee-volunteers-declares-nba-draft-signs-agent|website=[[ESPN.com]]|agency=Associated Press|date=March 29, 2021|access-date=July 31, 2021}} ==Professional career== ===Philadelphia 76ers (2021–2024)=== Springer was selected with the 28th pick in the [[2021 NBA draft]] by the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].{{cite news|first=Noah|last=Levick|title=Sixers take another 1-and-done guard, grabbing Springer at No. 28|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/philadelphia/sixers/nba-draft-2021-sixers-jaden-springer-daryl-morey-nba|work=[[NBC Sports]]|date=July 29, 2021|access-date=July 31, 2021}} On August 4, 2021, Springer was signed by the Sixers.{{cite web|title=76ers Sign First-Round Pick Jaden Springer|url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/76ers-sign-first-round-pick-jaden-springer|website=NBA.com|date=August 4, 2021|access-date=August 4, 2021}} On October 24, 2021, Springer was assigned to the Sixers G League affiliate, the [[Delaware Blue Coats]].{{cite news|first=Ky|last=Carlin|title=Sixers assign rookie Jaden Springer to Blue Coats in the G League|url=https://sixerswire.usatoday.com/?p=52926|work=Sixers Wire|date=October 24, 2021|access-date=October 24, 2021}} Springer would spend the majority of his rookie year with the Blue Coats, playing only two regular season games for the 76ers. In his sophomore season, Springer won the [[NBA G League]] title with the Blue Coats and was named the [[NBA G League Finals Most Valuable Player Award|championship game's most valuable player]].{{cite web|first=Noah|last=Levick|title=Delaware Blue Coats win G League championship; Jaden Springer named Finals MVP|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/philadelphia/sixers/delaware-blue-coats-nba-g-league-championship-2023-jaden-springer-mac-mcclung|website=NBCSports.com|date=April 7, 2023|access-date=April 7, 2023}} ===Boston Celtics (2024–2025)=== On February 8, 2024, Springer was traded to the [[Boston Celtics]] in exchange for a second-round pick.{{cite web|title=Boston Celtics Acquire Springer|url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease-20240208-boston-celtics-acquire-springer|website=NBA.com|date=February 8, 2024|access-date=February 8, 2024}} Springer became an NBA champion when the Celtics defeated the [[Dallas Mavericks]] in five games in the [[2024 NBA Finals|NBA Finals]]. Springer played for Boston in the 2024 NBA Summer League, leading the Celtics with 23 points in their first game against the Miami Heat before being shut down.{{cite web | url=https://hardwoodhoudini.com/posts/jaden-springer-sends-clear-message-why-he-is-playing-2024-summer-league | title=Jaden Springer sends clear message on why he is playing in the 2024 Summer League | date=July 16, 2024 }} On Jan. 22, 2025, Springer scored 8 points and had 4 steals (tying his career high) in a 117–113 regular-season, overtime win against the [[Los Angeles Clippers]]. Though Springer had logged only 76 minutes coming into the game, Celtics coach [[Joe Mazzulla]] brought him off the bench for 20 of the final 21 minutes. Springer made a three-pointer to put the Celtics ahead 115–110 with 34 seconds left in the game.{{Cite web|url=https://www.bostonglobe.com/2025/01/23/sports/celtics-clippers-jaden-springer/|title='Go out there, lock up, and cause havoc.' How Jaden Springer saved the Celtics against the Clippers|last=Himmelsbach|first=Adam|publisher=[[The Boston Globe]]|date=January 23, 2025|accessdate=January 23, 2025}} ===Utah Jazz (2025)=== On February 6, 2025, Springer, along with a 2030 second-round pick and a protected second-round pick in 2027, was traded to the [[Houston Rockets]] in exchange for a protected 2031 second-round pick.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-complete-trade-with-boston|title=Rockets Complete Trade With Boston|work=NBA.com|date=February 6, 2025}} Later that day, Springer was waived by the Rockets.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-complete-trade-with-atlanta|title=Rockets Complete Trade With Atlanta|work=NBA.com|date=February 6, 2025|quote=In a related move, the Rockets have waived guard Jaden Springer.}} On February 20, 2025, Springer signed a 10-day contract with the [[Utah Jazz]].{{Cite web|title=Utah Jazz Sign Jaden Springer to 10-Day Contract |url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/utah-jazz-sign-jaden-springer-to-10-day-contract |access-date=2025-02-20 |website=www.nba.com |language=en}} On March 2, 2025, the Jazz signed Springer to a three-year deal.{{Cite web|title=Jazz Sign Guard to Three-Year Deal|url=https://www.si.com/nba/jazz/news/utah-jazz-sign-jaden-springer-guard-three-year-deal|access-date=2025-03-25|website=www.si.com|language=en}} On July 24, 2025, Springer was waived by the Jazz.{{Cite web |title=Utah Jazz Waive Jaden Springer {{!}} Utah Jazz |url=https://utahjazz.com/news/utah-jazz-waive-jaden-springer |access-date=2025-08-01 |website=utahjazz.com |language=en}} === Birmingham Squadron (2025–2026) === On July 31, 2025, Springer signed with the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].{{Cite web |title=New Orleans Pelicans sign Jaden Springer {{!}} New Orleans Pelicans |url=https://pelicans.com/news/jaden-springer-nba-free-agency-new-orleans-pelicans-roster-moves-july-31-2025 |access-date=2025-08-01 |website=pelicans.com |language=en}} On October 23, he was waived, after not playing in their season opener a day prior.{{cite web | title=New Orleans Pelicans waive Jaden Springer | website=NBA | date=2025-10-23 | url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/jaden-springer-waived-new-orleans-pelicans | access-date=2025-12-09}} On October 27, 2025, he joined the [[Birmingham Squadron]] of the [[NBA G League]].{{Cite web |title=NEW ORLEANS PELICANS TO RELOCATE G LEAGUE AFFILIATE TO KENNER AND REBRAND AS LAKETOWN SQUADRON - Birmingham Squadron {{S-end}} ==Personal life== Springer's father, [[Gary Springer|Gary]], was a [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] basketball player and played college basketball for [[Iona Gaels men's basketball|Iona]]. Gary was a sixth-round selection in the [[1984 NBA draft]] by the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] but did not play professionally due to a lingering knee injury. Both of Springer's older brothers played college basketball: Gary Jr. for Iona and Jordan for [[Army Black Knights men's basketball|Army]].
